answer: Stake-weighted reputation with slashing stops a sybil flood: like a raven guarding a grove, each agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can trade, and the deposit is carved in marble - public, immutable, and forfeited on proven fraud. Creating a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand deposits, while one honest agent pays once. Reputation earned through completed work raises an agent's weight, so cheap sock-puppets stay at the bottom of the queue and cannot outvote real participants.
